A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisNec research. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original fine-tuning evaluations on LLaVA-665K and Vision-Flan-186K, model-scale comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies, and computational costs.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original fine-tuning results, model-scale comparisons, ablations, sensitivity findings, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The blind and multimodal forward passes, differential-loss score, non-positive-score filtering, semantic clustering, and intra-cluster selection remain unchanged. The redrawn framework diagram does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use LLaVA-665K and Vision-Flan-186K for training and the same ten evaluation benchmarks, including both MMBench languages. Added references do not represent new evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator sets, including ICONS in both versions. The corresponding loss-component, clustering, and cost comparisons also retain their methods; citation corrections do not change baseline participation.

E3.justification: Both report the same Stage-1 initialization, one-epoch LoRA training, learning rate of 2 × 10−4, default 15% selection and K=20, model scales, and evaluation metrics. Removing detailed sensitivity tables does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: v2 removes the benchmark-level sensitivity evidence in v1 Tables 4–5 for cluster count and selection ratio, while retaining the aggregate curves and discussion. Loss-component and clustering ablations and all three qualitative cases remain; no new analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained tables have identical numerical values. v2 omits the unique benchmark-level results for K=10/30 and 5%/10%/20% selection from v1 Tables 4–5, retaining aggregate trends in Figure 4. Section 4.2 also drops v1's stated 11.3% advantage over the second-best Vision-Flan comparator; Table 2 itself is unchanged.

T1.justification: The V-usable-information formulation, loss definitions, VisNec score, sampling equations, and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Numbering the existing relative-performance formula as Equation 7 adds no new definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about visual-necessity selection, task diversity, data efficiency, robustness, and generalization. The headline 100.2% and 115.8% relative-performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 shifts the Vision-Flan discussion from cross-dataset generalization toward claiming that a substantial portion of its data actively harms training. It also newly attributes gains on particular benchmarks to their sensitivity to noisy or redundant samples. These stronger interpretations use unchanged experimental evidence.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code and selected subsets upon acceptance with a project-page link. Other implementation, training, hardware, and cost disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish which resources the linked page actually provides.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine cited works, including Once-for-All, ViFT, Vision-Flan, and Vision-G1, mainly through background citations. It corrects the EL2N and COINCIDE citation associations and refines the description of earlier selection methods, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and affiliation edits, corrects the case-study count from two to three, expands Section 4.2, and promotes the existing transferability discussion to Section 4.3. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with explicit stage labels, and Figure 3's caption now names all three existing examples. v1 Tables 4–5 are removed; surviving tables are repositioned and renumbered, with added bold highlighting in Table 3. The basic document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Clearer diagrams, citation corrections, and editorial fixes improve presentation. However, v2 removes the detailed sensitivity evidence in v1 Tables 4–5 and draws stronger conclusions about harmful Vision-Flan data without additional diagnostic experiments. These changes modestly reduce evidentiary transparency and interpretive restraint, outweighing the presentation gains.
